scan.matching: Each file is read as bytes. A primitive is listed for a file when its token pattern matches the lower-cased bytes at an accepted position or one of its wrapper symbols occurs as a whole identifier. A position is accepted unless the byte before it is in `not_preceded_by`; with `camel_case` a match that starts with an upper-case letter directly after a lower-case letter or digit is accepted as well. A wrapper symbol is a case-sensitive pattern, optionally limited to paths, anchored on the definition that reaches the primitive. A file-granularity unit records the primitive set of every file; a tree-granularity unit records one primitive set for all its files.
scan.exclude_reason: The checker, its reference modules and its tests name every primitive as data. They are still scanned for pinned commitment values and commitment types.

scope.tree_unit_default: Every other scanned file belongs to the tree unit `<package>#other`, where the package is `crates/<name>` or the top-level directory.
scope.file_unit: A path under a listed prefix belongs to the file-granularity unit `<package>#zk`, unless a tree-unit override that applies inside the proof crates matches it. A path under one of the path roots belongs to that unit when its lower-cased form matches the pattern or the file names one of `file_granularity_primitives`, unless a tree-unit override matches it. Tooling directories (scripts, xtask, ci, tools, pytests, examples) are always tree units.

producer_ledger.purpose: Caller-level ledger of native digests for the four consumers the H.1 acceptance names (catalog, Kaigi, spentness, MKHE) and the privacy model they share: every production function whose own body calls a digest, with the primitives it calls, the domain literals it names, its return type and its role.
producer_ledger.method: Lexical (scripts/zk_rust_lexical_index.py). A function is listed when its body, without nested functions, matches a detector. A file is production when a chain of `mod` declarations without a test attribute reaches it from the crate root; a function is test-only when a test attribute guards it or an enclosing block. producer_ledger.limits: A function that only forwards to a listed producer is not listed. A digest reached through a macro or through a constant of another file has no domain literal here. Test-only producers are counted per file, not listed.

canonical_native_commitment.status: H.1 candidate, conditional on the security requirement of every role that moves. H.2 freezes the selection and the cross-SDK vectors; F.5 implements it. Nothing in the tree uses the frame yet.
canonical_native_commitment.applies_to: Commitments that are hashed natively and never recomputed inside a proof relation: the catalog commitment, the Kaigi authorization identities, the statement, parameter, release and receipt identities of MKHE and of the privacy model, and, provisionally, the confidential spentness tree, with their schemas, SDKs and fixtures.
decision_rule: If every changing role accepts a generic quantum collision estimate near 85 bits, the canonical native commitment is raw BLAKE3-256.

If any changing role requires at least 128 bits against quantum collision search, that role, or all of them for uniformity, uses an analysed 384-bit sponge: SHAKE256 with 48 bytes of output over the same frame. The tree already holds a byte-framed SHA3-384 owner for the privacy STARK substrate.

GoldilocksDigest384V1 is not the native default: it is slower natively by orders of magnitude and specs/fastpq_compact_digest_security.md records it as unqualified. It stays only where a Goldilocks relation recomputes it.
The existing 48-byte wire width is not a reason to keep a digest.

A digest that is recomputed inside a relation keeps a native-field algebraic hash; every bridge between a native commitment and an in-circuit digest is specified explicitly, and an unconstrained native digest is never treated as equal to the bytes it commits to.

A native commitment whose value is a domain field, a seed or a public input of a proof moves only in the same cutover as that proof profile (decision `changes-with-profile`); the transcript-seed check of each role records which case holds.

security_rationale.estimates: Ideal-hash estimates, not qualification claims: 128 bits against classical collision search, about 85 bits against quantum collision search (Brassard-Hoyer-Tapp), 256 bits against classical and 128 bits against quantum preimage search.
security_rationale.labels: A composition is labelled by its weakest property. A protocol labelled pq-qrom that relies on collision resistance of a 256-bit commitment is not a 128-bit post-quantum composition; H.2 either accepts the lower estimate in the label or selects the 384-bit sponge for that role.
security_rationale.framing: Domain separation comes from the frame, not from keyed or derive-key modes, so every SDK needs only the unkeyed hash.
security_rationale.review_state: BLAKE3 inherits the analysis of BLAKE2 with a reduced round count; SHAKE256 is FIPS 202. Neither statement is a review of this composition.

cost_rationale.summary: A byte-oriented digest is one compression call per 64 bytes with vector implementations on every supported platform; the six-lane algebraic digest runs 6 x 65 field rounds for every 14 input bytes.
cost_rationale.exploratory_measurement: See exploratory_measurements; single machine, single run, guidance only.
cost_rationale.in_circuit: The candidate is never opened in a relation, so it adds no constraint cost. A role that later needs an in-circuit opening leaves the candidate (see provisional).

exploratory_measurements.source_commit: d651d51715fd16881b34d75384c4b9ea95cbd229 with the uncommitted working tree of this task
exploratory_measurements.hardware: Apple M1 Ultra, 20 cores, 128 GiB, macOS 27.0.1
exploratory_measurements.conditions: One run on a machine shared with other builds; one thread; best of five batches (20,000 digests per batch, 200 for the six-lane digest); warm caches; thermal state and load not recorded; std::time::Instant, not the iroha_measurement harness. One-shot digest of a message of the stated length; the six-lane digest includes its domain frame, the others hash the bare message. The SHAKE256 figure is taken through the RustCrypto extendable-output reader; the verification of this task attributes the gap to SHA3-384 at 64 bytes (485 against 248 ns) to an extra permutation in that reader, which a fixed 48-byte squeeze does not need. No fixed-output SHAKE256 was timed, so SHA3-384 on the same run is the closer estimate of a 384-bit sponge.
exploratory_measurements.reading: On this run the six-lane digest costs about 6,000 times the candidate at 64 bytes and about 1,900 times at 4,096 bytes. A 384-bit sponge costs about 2 to 4 times the candidate (SHA3-384: 248 against 77 ns at 64 bytes, 8,855 against 2,430 ns at 4,096 bytes); the SHAKE256 reader figure at 64 bytes is higher for the reason stated under conditions. The byte-oriented digests are within a small factor of each other, so the choice among them rests on the security requirement, not on native cost.

bn254_poseidon.construction: Original Poseidon (not Poseidon2) over the BN254 scalar field: x^5, dense Cauchy MDS, widths 3 (rate 2) and 6 (rate 5), 8 full and 56 partial rounds for both widths, first Cauchy candidate (secure_mds = 0).
method: The reference script regenerates all 621 field elements with its own Grain LFSR and Cauchy construction and compares them with the Rust table.

The same generator run with the published round numbers reproduces pinned constants of the published BN254 width-three instantiation, so the generator is anchored to published values and not only to the repository table.
Every square minor of both matrices is checked, with three bounded linear-layer screens for one active S-box per partial round.
The paper's round-number inequalities for x^5 at a 128-bit target are evaluated with the objective of the fewest S-boxes and the margin of two full rounds and 7.5% partial rounds.
The Rust test runs the owner over vectors the script computed with its own permutation.
bn254_poseidon.limits: Agreement of two implementations, nonzero minors and the bounded screens do not qualify the parameter set. The inequalities are transcribed from the paper; the original round-number script was not fetched. Parameters are not changed by this task.

defects.title: The width-three table is not the published BN254 instantiation
defects.evidence: The published BN254 x^5 width-three permutation (hadeshash poseidonperm_x5_254_3, also shipped as the bn256 parameters of the poseidon-primitives 0.2.0 test oracle) uses 57 partial rounds. The repository uses 56. The Grain seed binds the round count, so none of the 195 published round constants and none of the MDS entries equal the repository's. The repository's value satisfies the margin rule as evaluated here (minimum 56).
defects.effect: Outputs differ from every other BN254 Poseidon deployment that follows the published instantiation; no attack follows from the round count.

defects.title: The width-six round count is one partial round below the margin rule
defects.evidence: For width 6 the inequalities need 53 partial rounds with 6 full rounds; the margin gives 8 full and 57 partial rounds. The repository uses 8 and 56. This is the result of the transcribed inequalities, not of the fetched reference script, and it is not a demonstrated attack. No published BN254 width-six instantiation exists to compare constants with.
defects.effect: The width-six permutation has less than the recommended margin.

defects.title: The two- and six-input helpers are single permutations without capacity or domain separation
defects.evidence: hash2 starts from the state [a, b, 0] and hash6 fills all six state coordinates with inputs; both return coordinate 0 of one permutation. hash6 has no capacity element: for unrestricted field inputs a collision is found by inverting the permutation, so its collision resistance rests on every caller and every circuit restricting the inputs to 64-bit values. hash2_u64 and hash6_u64 return only the low 64 bits. Neither helper shares a domain word with the byte sponge.
defects.effect: A consumer that treats these helpers as general collision-resistant hashes over field elements, or the 64-bit forms as commitments, has a weaker guarantee than its label.

post_quantum.audit_result: Cargo.lock holds no Kyber-, Dilithium- or other pre-standard package. The locked packages implement the final standards: the tests reproduce the official known-answer response of every parameter set and the structural identities that distinguish FIPS 203 and FIPS 204 from the round-three algorithms. One post-quantum construction lives outside Cargo.lock: the Falcon-512 trapdoor arithmetic of the Bootle Lantern issuer, adapted in tree from rust-fn-dsa 0.3 (finding PQ-D3).
post_quantum.known_answer_method: Response `count = 0` of the NIST known-answer generator as PQClean prints it. scripts/zk_pq_kat_reference.py derives the randomness with its own AES-256 CTR_DRBG; the Rust tests feed it to the derandomized entry points and compare with the tracked response files. The official nistkat-sha256 values of the vendored PQClean metadata are pinned twice: in the script, which hashes each file with hashlib, and in the Rust tests, which hash the included file text with a test-only FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 and compare with the pinned value, so a regenerated response file cannot pass either check.

round_three_differences.ml-kem: Key generation hashes d with the rank byte; encapsulation uses m directly and returns the first half of G(m || H(ek)) without a further KDF; implicit rejection returns J(z || c). Public key, secret key and ciphertext lengths equal Kyber's, so a length check cannot tell the two apart.
round_three_differences.ml-dsa: Key generation hashes the seed with the matrix dimensions; tr is 64 bytes; signing binds a domain byte and a context string and is hedged. Round-three Dilithium secret keys were 2528, 4000 and 4864 bytes and signatures 2420, 3293 and 4595 bytes.

shared_transcript_requirements.status: Requirements for the shared backend transcript. H.2 selects the transcript from them and from the security design; no proof byte of an existing transcript is preserved for compatibility.
shared_transcript_requirements.candidate: A domain-separated SHAKE256 transcript with canonical framing and rejection sampling, chosen independently of the State tree hash. The committed q77 engine already derives its challenges from SHAKE256 tapes and commits with SHA3-256.
framing: Every absorbed object is framed with a role tag and an exact length; no two objects share a prefix-free ambiguity.
Field and extension-field challenges are decoded by rejection sampling from the output stream with a bounded retry count; a failed draw is a rejection, not a reduction.
Every challenge names its purpose in the frame, and its derivation covers the whole preceding transcript.
The requested output length is part of the input frame, so two lengths never share a prefix.

binding_order.binds: Protocol and profile identity, relation identity, field and extension, AIR geometry, degree and masking bounds, FRI schedule, and the complete public statement including State anchors, execution context and the role-specific replay domain.
The terminal polynomial and the grinding nonce.
The complete bounded openings and their authenticated indices.

shared_transcript_requirements.invariant: No challenge is derived before the commitments it tests.
grinding: The grinding predicate covers the whole preceding transcript and one frozen difficulty per profile.

A difficulty of d bits costs about 2^d classical hash evaluations and about 2^(d/2) quantum oracle steps under idealized search; neither figure is a soundness bound, and work-security is accounted separately from algebraic and FRI error.
The nonce width and the search bound are fixed, so a prover cannot grind across statement variants.

security_claims.classical_rom: A classical random-oracle claim needs the round-by-round soundness of the interactive protocol and the query budget; algebraic and FRI error sums alone do not establish Fiat-Shamir security or hiding.
security_claims.qrom: A quantum random-oracle claim needs its own reduction for a multi-round STARK. Results for specific protocol classes do not transfer automatically; until such a reduction is supplied the claim stays open and the label is not pq-qrom on the strength of the hash alone.
security_claims.separation: Interactive algebraic and FRI error, Fiat-Shamir loss, commitment binding, grinding and hiding are stated separately and the claimed level is the weakest of them.
